{{Short description|British astrophysicist and author (born 1947)}}
[[Image:DField - Winter 2005.jpg|thumb|right|David Field]]
'''David Field''' (born 17 June 1947) is an [[astrophysics|astrophysicist]] and author, living in [[Århus]], Denmark.

== Education ==
The son of [[E._J._Field|E.J.]] and Dereen, Field studied Chemistry at [[Newcastle University]], UK, followed by a PhD at the [[University of Cambridge]]. He was later awarded the degree of [[Doctor of Science]] by the University of Cambridge. Previously Reader in Physical Chemistry at the [[University of Bristol]], he now researches astrophysics and experimental physics as a professor at the [[University of Aarhus]]. He has published over 175 papers in this subject.<ref>[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/nph-abs_connect?return_req=no_params&&author=Field,+D&db_key=AST Astronomical Data System]</ref>  He is on the editorial board of [[Astrobiology (journal)|Astrobiology]], and played a key role in the discovery of [[spontelectrics]].

== Authorship ==
Aside from academic work, Field is also known for his writing, being the author of a successful fiction series that begins with ''[[Friends and Enemies]]'', and a second novel ''[[Beings in a Dream]]''. The third and final volume in this trilogy, ''[[The Fairest Star]]'', was published in November 2008.
